ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the skeletal arrangement of SO3, with S in the middle and three O atoms distributed on the left side, right side, and below, indicating the basic framework in which the sulfur atom is connected to three oxygen atoms. Reasoning: The number of valence electrons in neutral SO3 is S's 6 plus the 18 from 3 O atoms, for a total of 24. After making S connect to three O atoms according to the skeleton in the figure, in order to minimize formal charges, and allowing sulfur to expand its octet, the best Lewis structure can be drawn as three S=O double bonds, with the formal charge of each atom being 0. Therefore under this model the bond order of each S–O bond is 2, so the statement claiming that the S–O bond order is 5/3 is false. The question asks for the S–O bond order falsely claimed in the false statement, so the answer is 5/3.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows an SO3 skeleton with S central and three surrounding O atoms. From the text, construct the Lewis structure for neutral SO3 and identify which claimed S-O bond order is incorrect. Count 6 valence electrons from S plus 3×6 from O = 24. Connect S to all three O atoms as suggested by the image, then adjust lone pairs/bonds to minimize formal charges. Because sulfur can expand its octet, the best Lewis structure has three S=O double bonds, giving formal charges of zero on all atoms and S-O bond order 2. Therefore, the statement whose S-O bond order claim is wrong is the one claiming the S-O bond order is 5/3.
